evals.name: vague-gradual-wakeup
evals.prompt: I'm building a wake-up / alarm app for iOS. I want to add a feature where the alarm helps users wake up gradually. Can you help me design and implement it?
evals.expected_output: Surfaces ambiguity ('gradually' = light? sound? duration?) before writing code. Walks through Phase 1 (Requirements) with testable acceptance criteria. Produces a basic-design document. Does not jump straight into implementation.

assertions.text: Produces a basic-design document file (e.g. basic-design.md) under outputs/
Surfaces ambiguity about 'gradually' explicitly (mentions at least two of: sound volume, light, vibration, duration) in the transcript or design doc
Acceptance criteria are stated in measurable / testable form (specific numbers, durations, or observable conditions — not just adjectives like 'fast' or 'pleasant')
Does not write the implementation code before requirements and basic-design are written down (design-first ordering)
Treats this as a LOCAL feature: documents a Swift interface contract (public types / use-case protocols, e.g. from interface-contract.md) and does NOT invent a REST/OpenAPI contract for it
The transcript names which phase / gate the run is at and which would block on human input in a real session

evals.name: specific-snooze-feature
evals.prompt: Add a snooze feature to my alarm screen. The behavior: when the alarm fires, show a 'Snooze' button. Tapping it silences the alarm for 5 minutes, then the alarm fires again. Maximum 3 snoozes per alarm. After the 3rd snooze, the button is hidden so only 'Dismiss' is available. Please drive this through to a working implementation.
evals.expected_output: Derives testable acceptance criteria, produces basic-design and detail-design documents, drives TDD cycles (tests → impl → refactor), sets up parallel verification design.

assertions.text: Produces a basic-design document file under outputs/ that includes a Scope and a Data model section
Produces a detail-design document file under outputs/
The data model captures the snooze count and the rule 'max 3' (numeric limit and reset semantics described)
Includes at least one unit test file or test sketch covering snooze behavior
Implementation follows a TDD ordering: tests are present and the transcript describes test → implement → refactor rather than implement-first
Treats this as a LOCAL feature: the interface contract is the public Swift surface (types / use-case protocol), not an OpenAPI/REST document
Transcript names at least one phase gate check (Phase 2 → 3, or Phase 3a → 4) and what evidence satisfied it
Verification design (UI / E2E checks) is mentioned as a parallel track to implementation, mapped to acceptance criteria

evals.name: premature-implementation-pushback
evals.prompt: I want to ship a 'send wake-up greeting' feature today — when the alarm goes off and the user dismisses it, automatically post 'Good morning!' to their connected Slack workspace. Just code it up real quick, we can document later.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on 'just code it up' and 'document later'. Surfaces Slack auth, dismiss semantics, error handling. Drives Phase 1 before writing implementation.

assertions.text: Transcript explicitly pushes back on 'just code it up real quick' / 'document later', naming the cost of skipping design
Identifies Slack OAuth / authentication / credential storage as a missing requirement
Identifies at least two additional ambiguities (e.g. which channel, dismiss semantics, error handling if Slack API fails, what counts as 'connected workspace', offline behavior)
Drives Phase 1 (Requirements) — writing acceptance criteria — before writing implementation code
Produces a basic-design document file under outputs/ (even if partial) rather than only source code
Recognizes this is a NETWORK-boundary feature (Slack HTTP API) and treats the Slack call's contract accordingly (OpenAPI is appropriate here, unlike the local features)
Acceptance criteria are stated in measurable / testable form
